_note: Copy to docs/work/checklist/<yyyy-mm-dd>-<subject>.json. Never fill this file in place. status is pass|fail|skipped|substituted; substituted means checked by a different instrument than the item names, and its reason must say which. accepted stays null until a human answers it, so an unfinished run is visibly unfinished. Delete any item whose feature no longer exists rather than skipping it.

derived.note: Produced by scripts/derive-facts.py at run time, never typed from memory or a previous run.

findings-against-prior-runs: No prior run exists for this checklist copy (docs/work/checklist/ was empty), so nothing to contradict. Recording the shape for the next run: (a) the annotate tier's warning lives at data.warning, not meta — truncating the envelope makes it look like the tier never fired, which it did; (b) 'file#section' is an eval-corpus expectedSource format, NOT a query syntax, so an item worded as an anchor query tests a feature the product does not have.

items.expected-result: Release build and pack succeed; the global ai-raccoon tool force-updates to this build and `ai-raccoon --version` matches derived.version
items.observed-result: Installed tool reports derived.version AND carries the git SHA of main's merge commit 155f281e, so the running binary is provably the merged build, not a stale pack.
items.acceptance-reason: Version matches derived, and the +SHA suffix closes the 'force-update silently kept the previous build' gap by identity rather than by version string alone.

items.expected-result: `serve --port 0` binds and reports its port; `serve --restart` on that port cycles the server it finds rather than attaching, and never touches port 7721
items.command: ai-raccoon --data-root <scratch> --port 0 serve ; then --port 7788 serve ; then --port 7788 serve --restart
items.evidence:
serve --port 0 -> 'Now listening on: http://127.0.0.1:63461', mcp-token minted 0600.
serve --restart -> 'ai-raccoon: port 7788 is in use but gave the probe no answer; nothing was asked to stop' then IOException: Failed to bind ... address already in use. Incumbent pid unchanged (76062). Reproduced on both an ephemeral port (63461) and an explicit one (7788).
By hand: POST /mcp unauthenticated -> 401 with body {"jsonrpc":"2.0",...}; with the token -> 400 JSON-RPC. Endpoint answers in milliseconds.
items.observed-result: Start works (binds, mints the token). --restart does NOT cycle a live server: the probe reports no answer and the new process dies on AddressInUse. ServerProbe treats a body containing 'jsonrpc' as Answered and does not classify 401 as transient, yet the endpoint demonstrably returns exactly that instantly — so the verdict contradicts the endpoint's real behaviour.
items.acceptance-reason: Not accepted: --restart is unusable against any token-gated server, which is every server. Refusing to kill an unidentified listener is correct behaviour and the message is actionable, so this is a probe-verdict defect rather than a safety one. Root cause not traced here — the checklist finds what is broken; tracing why belongs elsewhere. Not previously tracked; needs an issue.

items.expected-result: memory_write returns a hash for a stored entry; a rejected write returns Stored=false with a reason and no fabricated hash (ADR-0032)
items.command: tools/call memory_write (clean prose) ; tools/call memory_write x3 (the three HermesProcessNoisePolicy shapes)
items.evidence:
clean -> {"hash":"c74e8583...","stored":true}
rejected x3 -> {"stored":false,"reason":"rejected by noise policy 'HermesBackgroundProcessLog'"}
items.observed-result: A stored write returns a real hash with stored=true; a rejected write returns stored=false and names the policy. No fabricated entry in either direction.
items.acceptance-reason: Both directions exercised, so the item can fail.

items.expected-result: memory_search returns the written entry through hybrid BM25 + vector RRF ranking
items.command: tools/call memory_search query='an antique navigation instrument reflecting evening light in a stargazing room'
items.evidence: hits: 1 -> hash c74e8583..., ranking 1, snippet 'The observatory kept a brass astrolabe on the sill, and by lamplight...'
items.observed-result: Query shares no literal term with the stored text (antique navigation instrument/astrolabe, evening light/lamplight, stargazing room/observatory) and still returns it at rank 1, so the vector leg is live.
items.acceptance-reason: Designed so BM25 alone cannot carry it; a dead vector leg would fail this item.

items.expected-result: memory_get returns the full entry for a hash reachable from the caller; an unknown hash refuses rather than returning empty (ADR-0035)
items.evidence: {"data":{"hash":"c74e8583...","value":"The observatory kept a brass astrolabe on the sill..."}}
items.observed-result: Returns the exact stored content for the hash.
items.acceptance-reason: Round-trips the value written in the write item.

items.expected-result: a `file#section` query returns that exact chunk within the production result window
items.command: settings ingest scope add ; memory_ingest_file sextant.md (3823 B, 2 sections) ; memory_search 'sextant.md#arc-calibration'
items.evidence:
ingest -> {"indexed":1}; entries for that path: (0,1,300B) AND (0..4, 5). Search returned chunk 2/5 and chunk 0/5 alongside the stale 0/1.
No '#'-anchor handling found in MemoryTools/the store, and none documented in docs/reference/agent-memory-server.md.
items.observed-result: Chunk-level retrieval works — search returns a specific chunk of a multi-chunk file with chunkIndex/totalChunks. But 'file#section' is NOT a query syntax: it is the eval corpus's expectedSource format, so the item as literally worded tests something the product does not offer. Separately, re-ingesting the SAME path with changed content left the previous chunk set in place (a 300-byte 0/1 row surviving beside the new 0..4/5), so search can return content no longer in the file.
items.acceptance-reason: Substituted: chunk resolution verified via chunkIndex/totalChunks on a deliberately over-budget fixture, because the '#section' query form does not exist. NOT accepted overall — the stale-chunk observation is a real defect found by this run and needs an issue. The watch digest path deletes-then-replaces by source path; the direct memory_ingest_file path appears not to.

items.expected-result: each registered write-path policy rejects what it claims to, the write reports the rejection, and the rejected content is retrievable from the noise store (ADR-0039)
items.command: memory_write x1 clean (negative control) + x3 notification shapes ; sqlite3 'select substr(request_content,1,40) from noise_entries'
items.evidence:
clean -> stored=true. Three shapes -> stored=false, 'rejected by noise policy HermesBackgroundProcessLog'. noise_entries holds exactly those 3 rows.
Registered policies in AppRegistrations: HermesProcessNoisePolicy only (ADR-0033 removed the rest).
items.observed-result: The one registered write-path policy rejects all three shapes it claims, accepts clean prose, and every rejection is retained in the noise store.
items.acceptance-reason: Negative control included, so a policy that rejected everything would fail this item. Steps were written against the policies actually registered, not a remembered list.

items.expected-result: the refuse and annotate tiers behave as ADR-0040 describes; the structural detector is off until `queryguard structural enable` and only ever annotates (ADR-0041)
items.command: memory_search with a Hermes notification (refuse tier), with a stack trace (warn tier), and sqlite3 settings for queryGuard.*
items.evidence:
refuse -> McpException 'invalid-params: This looks like tool output rather than a question...'
warn -> data.warning = 'This query contains what looks like log or stack-trace output...' (results still returned)
settings: no queryGuard rows; DefaultStructuralEnabled=false in QueryGuardConfigKeys.
items.observed-result: Refuse tier throws with actionable guidance; annotate tier returns results WITH a warning; the structural detector ships disabled and stays disabled absent an explicit setting.
items.acceptance-reason: All three tiers behave as ADR-0040/0041 specify. Note for future runs: the warning is at data.warning, not in meta — truncating the envelope makes the annotate tier look broken when it is not.

items.expected-result: memory_watch_status lists live registrations and their sync state
items.command: settings watch enable checklist true ; memory_watch_add ; memory_watch_status
items.evidence:
before enabling -> 'watching-disabled: Watching is disabled for project checklist.' and status []
after -> add returns the path; status -> 1 watch: {projectId: checklist, path: .../docs, state: Scanning}
items.observed-result: Status reflects live registrations, and reports an empty list truthfully when watching is disabled rather than pretending to register.
items.acceptance-reason: Both states observed (disabled-refusal and registered), so an always-empty response would fail.
